instruction: We act for Seles Lift Services, LLC, the buyer of Tripux Elevator Company's assets. Seles needs a clear view of where the transaction documents leave it exposed before we finalize them. Please review the asset purchase agreement (asset_purchase_agreement_seles_tripux.md) and the related agreed-form and ancillary documents in the folder: the escrow agreement (escrow_agreement_agreed_form.md), the key employee agreement with Renata Oyelaran (key_employee_agreement_oyelaran.md), and the transition services agreement (transition_services_agreement_agreed_form.md). The folder also holds a Fenmark Workwear Rentals uniform rental agreement (fenmark_uniform_rental_agreement.md). Please look at it and tell me whether it has any bearing on the deal. Prepare a memo to me listing each issue you find. For each one, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters for Seles, and recommend a fix. Please put the most significant points first, and flag anything you think needs to go back to the client before we respond to the other side.

rubric.text: The response identifies that Key Employee Agreement Section 8.3 requires Renata Oyelaran's prior written consent to assignment in a sale of substantially all assets. It states that without that consent the assignment is void and her restrictive covenants terminate. It also identifies that the APA's required-consent schedule (Section 4.4) and closing condition (Section 7.2(c)) do not cover this consent. The response locates the issue in Key Employee Agreement Section 8.3, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Buyer's February 23, 2026 objection to Schedule Supplement No. 1, which was delivered February 9, 2026, fell outside the 5-Business-Day objection window in APA Section 6.5. It also identifies that this lets Seller argue the inspection deficiencies are cured for indemnity purposes and claim the $640,000 Special Escrow. The response locates the issue in Escrow Agreement Section 3.3 (and/or APA Section 6.5), explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Indemnity Escrow Amount is $1,875,000.
The response states that the Special Escrow Amount is $640,000.
The response states that the purchase price under the APA is $18,750,000.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner. It presents the issues in an order the response describes or presents as most significant first.
The response expressly addresses the Fenmark Workwear Rentals uniform rental agreement and states whether it has any bearing on the deal.
The response claims that Buyer's February 23, 2026 objection to Schedule Supplement No. 1 was timely under APA Section 6.5.
The response claims that the 15-month claims period in the Escrow Agreement overrides or extends the APA's 90-day survival period for General Representations.
